stem: Overbrook Data's internal analytics API on API Gateway gets an unpredictable spike of traffic from one internal reporting job every night, and the team separately wants a configured ceiling so requests to the API never exceed the account-level throttling limit AWS enforces for the Region. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Increase the reporting job's EC2 instance size so it finishes faster
Request an AWS Support increase to the Region's account-level throttling limit
Configure a stage-level burst limit sized to absorb the nightly reporting job's traffic pattern
Leave throttling at the account-level default with no stage or usage-plan settings configured for this API
Configure a usage plan quota for the reporting job's API key set below the Region's account-level limit

rationale: A stage-level burst limit is exactly the setting built to absorb a short traffic spike like the nightly job. A usage plan quota set below the account-level limit gives the team a configured ceiling instead of depending on the fixed AWS-side limit. Resizing the reporting job's EC2 instance does not change the API's request rate at all. Raising the account-level limit through Support moves the ceiling upward for every API in the Region rather than giving this API a ceiling of its own. Leaving throttling at the account-level default means no stage or usage-plan setting exists to absorb the nightly spike, and the account-level limit is set by AWS and cannot be tuned per API.
